'''Henri Paul Cartan''' ({{IPA|fr|kaʁtɑ̃|lang}}; 8 July 1904 – 13 August 2008) was a French [[mathematician]] who made substantial contributions to [[algebraic topology]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Augereau |first=Jean-François |date=19 August 2008 |title=Henri Cartan, mathématicien |language=fr |trans-title=Henri Cartan, mathematician |work=[[Le Monde]] |url=https://www.lemonde.fr/disparitions/article/2008/08/19/henri-cartan-mathematicien_1085441_3382.html |access-date=16 April 2022}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite web |date=8 June 2004 |title=Communiqué de presse pour le centenaire d'Henri Cartan (2004) |trans-title=Press communication for the centenary of Henri Cartan (2004) |url=https://www.academie-sciences.fr/archivage_site/presse/communique/hommage_080704.pdf |website=[[Académie des Sciences]] |language=fr |access-date=19 April 2022 |archive-date=17 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220817220759/https://www.academie-sciences.fr/archivage_site/presse/communique/hommage_080704.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Weil |first=Martin |date=31 August 2008 |title=Noted French mathematician and teacher |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2008-aug-31-me-cartan31-story.html |access-date=25 April 2022 |website=[[Los Angeles Times]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

He was the son of the mathematician [[Élie Cartan]], nephew of mathematician [[Anna Cartan]], oldest brother of composer {{Interlanguage link|Jean Cartan|lt=Jean Cartan|fr|4=de}}, [[physicist]] {{Interlanguage link|Louis Cartan|lt=Louis Cartan|fr}} and mathematician {{Interlanguage link|Hélène Cartan|lt=Hélène Cartan|fr}}, and the son-in-law of physicist [[Pierre Weiss]].

==Life==
According to his own words, Henri Cartan was interested in mathematics at a very young age, without being influenced by his family.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Jackson |first=Allyn |year=1999 |title=Interview with Henri Cartan |url=https://www.ams.org/notices/199907/fea-cartan.pdf |journal=[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]] |volume=46 |issue=7 |pages=782–788}}</ref> He moved to [[Paris]] with his family after his father's appointment at [[Sorbonne University|Sorbonne]] in 1909 and he attended secondary school at [[Lycée Hoche]] in [[Versailles, Yvelines|Versailles]].<ref name=":4">{{MacTutor Biography|id=Cartan_Henri}}</ref><ref name=":5">{{Cite news |year=2008 |title=Henri Cartan: mathematician |language=en |work=[[The Times]] |url=https://www.thetimes.com/comment/register/article/henri-cartan-mathematician-j2d2jc939wt |access-date=18 April 2022 |issn=0140-0460}} available also at {{Cite news |title=Henri Cartan – Times obituary |language=en |website=[[MacTutor History of Mathematics archive]] |url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Obituaries/Cartan_Times/ |access-date=18 April 2022}}</ref>

In 1923 he started studying mathematics at [[École Normale Supérieure]], receiving an [[agrégation]] in 1926 and a doctorate in 1928.<ref name=":4" /><ref name=":5" /> His PhD thesis, entitled ''Sur les systèmes de fonctions holomorphes à variétés linéaires lacunaires et leurs applications'', was supervised by [[Paul Montel]].<ref name=":1">{{MathGenealogy|id=49555}}</ref>

Cartan taught at [[Lycée Malherbe]] in [[Caen]] from 1928 to 1929, at the [[University of Lille]] from 1929 to 1931 and at the [[University of Strasbourg]] from 1931 to 1939. After the [[German invasion of France (1940)|German invasion of France]] the university staff was moved to [[Clermont Ferrand]]. He recommended the mathematicians [[Marie-Hélène Schwartz]] and [[Laurent Schwartz]] move to work at the University of Strasbourg in Clermont Ferrand for both their research and for their safety.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Marie-Hélène Schwartz - Biography |url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Schwartz_Marie-Helene/ |access-date=2026-06-07 |website=Maths History |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Laurent Schwartz - Biography |url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Schwartz/ |access-date=2026-06-07 |website=Maths History |language=en}}</ref> In 1940 he returned to Paris to work at [[University of Paris|Université de Paris]] and École Normale Supérieure.<ref name=":5" /> From 1969 until his retirement in 1975 he was professor at [[Paris-Sud University]].<ref name=":4" /> 

Cartan died on 13 August 2008 at the age of 104. His funeral took place the following Wednesday on 20 August in [[Die, Drome]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=18 August 2008 |title=Décès du mathématicien français Henri Cartan |language=fr |trans-title=Death of French mathematician Henri Cartan |website=[[L'Obs]] |url=https://www.nouvelobs.com/societe/20080818.OBS7733/deces-du-mathematicien-francais-henri-cartan.html |access-date=18 April 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Chang |first=Kenneth |date=25 August 2008 |title=Henri Cartan, French Mathematician, Is Dead at 104 |language=en-US |work=[[The New York Times]] |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/08/25/science/25cartan.html |access-date=16 April 2022 |issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=18 August 2008 |title=Décès d'Henri Cartan, mathématicien français |trans-title=Decease of Henri Cartan, French mathematician |url=https://www.france24.com/fr/20080818-deces-dhenri-cartan-mathematicien-francais-math%C3%A9matiques |access-date=25 April 2022 |publisher=[[France 24]] |language=fr}}</ref>

of the [[International Mathematical Union|International Mathematics Union]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=IMU Executive Committee |url=https://www.mathunion.org/organization/imu-executive-committee == Political and social activities ==
During the 70's and the 80's Cartan used his influence to help obtain the release of several dissident mathematicians, including [[Leonid Plyushch]], imprisoned by the [[Soviet Union]], [[Jose Luis Massera]], imprisoned between 1975 and 1984 by the [[Civic-military dictatorship of Uruguay|Uruguayan dictatorship]], and [[Sion Assidon]], imprisoned during the [[Years of Lead (Morocco)|Moroccan Years of Lead]]. For his humanitarian efforts, he received in 1989 the [[Heinz R. Pagels Human Rights of Scientists Award]] from the [[New York Academy of Sciences]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":7">{{Cite journal |last1=Serre |first1=Jean-Pierre |author-link=Jean-Pierre Serre |year=2009 |title=Henri Paul Cartan. 8 July 1904 – 13 August 2008 |journal=[[Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society]] |volume=55 |pages=37–44 |doi=10.1098/rsbm.2009.0005 |doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name=":8">{{Cite journal |last=Serre |first=Jean-Pierre |author-link=Jean-Pierre Serre |year=2014 |title=Obituary: Henri Cartan 1904-2008 |journal=Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society |language=en |volume=46 |issue=1 |pages=211–216 |doi=10.1112/blms/bdt079|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name=":9">{{Cite journal |last1=Bourguignon |first1=Jean-Pierre |author-link=Jean-Pierre Bourguignon |last2=Hirzebruch |first2=Friedrich |author-link2=Friedrich Hirzebruch |last3=Remmert |first3=Reinhold |author-link3=Reinhold Remmert |year=2010 |title=Cartan, Europe, and Human Rights |url=https://www.ams.org/notices/201008/rtx100800972p.pdf |journal=[[Notices of the AMS]] |publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]] |volume=57 |issue=8 |pages=972–975}}</ref>

Since the 30's Cartan had tight collaborations with many German mathematicians, including [[Heinrich Behnke]] and [[Peter Thullen]]. Right after [[World War II]] he put many efforts to improve the cooperation between French and German mathematicians and restore the flow of exchanges of ideas and students.<ref name=":9" /><ref>{{Cite news |last=Ziegler |first=Günter |author-link=Günter M. Ziegler |year=2009 |title=Der französische Freund |language=de |trans-title=The French friend |website=[[Die Zeit]] |url=https://www.zeit.de/online/2008/34/henri-cartan-nachruf |access-date=27 November 2025}}</ref>

Cartan supported the idea of [[European Federalism]] and from 1974 to 1985 was president of the French section of the [[Union of European Federalists]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Archives de l'UEF-France et mémoire du fédéralisme |trans-title=Archives of the UEF-France and memories of federalism |url=https://www.uef.fr/archives-de-l-uef-france-et-memoire-du-federalisme |access-date=25 April 2022 |website=uef.fr |date=31 October 2015 |language=fr}}</ref> At the [[1984 European elections]] he was the leader of the ''Liste pour les États-Unis d'Europe'',<ref name=":0" /> which obtained 0.4% of votes and did not elect any candidate.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Mabille |first=Xavier |year=1984 |title=Les résultats des élections européennes de juin 1984 |trans-title=The results of the European elections of June 1984 |url=http://www.cairn.info/revue-courrier-hebdomadaire-du-crisp-1984-18-page-1.htm?ref=doi |journal=Courrier Hebdomadaire du CRISP |language=fr |volume=1043 |issue=18 |pages=1–31 |doi=10.3917/cris.1043.0001 |issn=0008-9664|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

In 1992 he gave a speech at the first [[European Congress of Mathematics]] in Paris, remarking the common heritage and future of European countries and praising the first reunion between mathematicians from the two [[Iron Curtain|previously separated]] parts of Europe.<ref name=":9" />

== Research ==
Cartan worked in several fields across [[algebra]], [[geometry]] and [[Mathematical analysis|analysis]], focusing primarily on [[algebraic topology]] and [[homological algebra]].<ref name=":7" /><ref name=":8" />

He was a founding member of the [[Nicolas Bourbaki|Bourbaki group]] in 1934 and one of its most active participants. After 1945 he started his own [[French mathematical seminars|seminar]] in Paris, which deeply influenced [[Jean-Pierre Serre]], [[Armand Borel]], [[Alexander Grothendieck]] and [[Frank Adams]], amongst others of the leading lights of the younger generation. The number of his official students was small, but includes [[Joséphine Guidy Wandja]] (the first African woman to gain a PhD in mathematics),<ref>{{Cite web |title=Joséphine Guidy-Wandja |url=https://www.mathunion.org/cwm/people/gallery/josephine-guidy-wandja |access-date=2023-03-25 |website=[[International Mathematical Union]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Cassiau-Haurie |first=Christophe |date=2008-02-20 |title=Les femmes peinent à percer les bulles |trans-title=Women struggle to break through bubbles |url=https://africultures.com/les-femmes-peinent-a-percer-les-bulles-7367/ |access-date=2023-03-25 |website=Africultures |language=fr-FR}}</ref> [[Adrien Douady]], [[Roger Godement]], [[Max Karoubi]], [[Jean-Louis Koszul]], Jean-Pierre Serre and [[René Thom]].<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":3" />

Cartan's first research interests, until the 40's, were in the theory of [[functions of several complex variables]], which later gave rise to the theory of [[Complex variety|complex varieties]] and [[Algebraic geometry and analytic geometry|analytic geometry]]. Motivated by the solution to the [[Cousin problems]], he worked on [[sheaf cohomology]] and [[coherent sheaves]] and [[mathematical proof|proved]] two powerful results, [[Cartan's theorems A and B]].

Since the 50's he became more interested in [[algebraic topology]]. Among his major contributions, he worked on [[cohomology operation]]s and [[Homology (mathematics)|homology]] of the [[Eilenberg–MacLane space]]s,<ref>{{Cite web |date=1954–1955 |title=Séminaire Henri Cartan, Tome 7 |trans-title=Seminar Henri Cartan |url=http://www.numdam.org/volume/SHC_1954-1955__7/ |access-date=25 April 2022 |website=numdam.org |language=fr |archive-date=25 April 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220425232321/http://www.numdam.org/volume/SHC_1954-1955__7/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> he introduced the notion of [[Steenrod algebra]],<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Cartan |first=Henri |year=1955 |title=Sur l'itération des opérations de Steenrod |trans-title=On the iteration of Steenrod operations |url=https://link.springer.com/10.1007/BF02564270 |journal=[[Commentarii Mathematici Helvetici]] |language=fr |volume=29 |issue=1 |pages=40–58 |doi=10.1007/BF02564270 |s2cid=124558011 |issn=0010-2571|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and, together with Jean-Pierre Serre, developed the method of "killing [[homotopy group]]s".<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Cartan |first1=Henri |title=Espaces fibrés et groupes d'homotopie. I. Constructions générales |journal=[[Comptes Rendus de l'Académie des Sciences, Série I]] |volume=234 |pages=288–290 |year=1952a |place=Paris |issn=0764-4442 |mr=0046045 |last2=Serre |first2=Jean-Pierre |author1-link=Henri Cartan |author2-link=Jean-Pierre Serre}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Cartan |first1=Henri |title=Espaces fibrés et groupes d'homotopie. II. Applications |journal=Comptes Rendus de l'Académie des Sciences, Série I |volume=234 |pages=393–395 |year=1952b |place=Paris |issn=0764-4442 |mr=0046046 |last2=Serre |first2=Jean-Pierre |author1-link=Henri Cartan |author2-link=Jean-Pierre Serre}}</ref> His 1956 book with [[Samuel Eilenberg]] on homological algebra<ref>{{cite book |author=Cartan |first1=Henri |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=0268b52ghcsC |title=Homological Algebra |last2=Eilenberg |first2=Samuel |publisher=[[Princeton University Press]] |year=1956|author-link2=Samuel Eilenberg}} {{isbn|0691049912 }}.</ref> was an important text, treating the subject with a moderate level of abstraction with the help of [[category theory]].<ref>{{cite journal |author=Mac Lane, Saunders |author-link=Saunders Mac Lane |year=1956 |title=Review: ''Homological algebra'', by Henri Cartan and Samuel Eilenberg |url=https://www.ams.org/journals/bull/1956-62-06/S0002-9904-1956-10082-7/ |journal=[[Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.]] |volume=62 |issue=6 |pages=615–624 |doi=10.1090/S0002-9904-1956-10082-7 |doi-access=free}}</ref> They introduced fundamental concepts, including those of [[projective module]], [[weak dimension]], and what is now called the [[Cartan–Eilenberg resolution]].

Among his other contributions, in [[general topology]] he introduced the notions of [[filter (mathematics)|filter]] and [[ultrafilter]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Cartan |first=Henri |year=1937 |title=Théorie des filtres |trans-title=Theory of filters |url=http://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k3157c/f594.image |journal=[[Comptes Rendus de l'Académie des Sciences]] |language=fr |volume=205 |pages=595–598}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Cartan |first=Henri |year=1937 |title=Filtres et ultrafiltres |trans-title=Filters and ultrafilters |url=http://gallica.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/bpt6k3157c/f776.image |journal=[[Comptes Rendus de l'Académie des Sciences]] |language=fr |volume=205 |pages=777–779}}</ref> and in [[potential theory]] he developed the [[Fine topology (potential theory)|fine topology]] and proved [[Cartan's lemma (potential theory)|Cartan's lemma]]. The [[Cartan model]] for [[equivariant cohomology]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Cartan |first=Henri |year=1950 |title=La transgression dans un groupe de Lie et dans un espace fibré principal |trans-title=Transgression in a Lie group and in a principal fibre bundle |url=https://zbmath.org/?q=an%3A0045.30701 |journal=Colloque de topologie (Espaces fibrés). Bruxelles |language=fr |pages=57–71 |zbl=0045.30701}}</ref> is also named after him.
